dedupe_keys.name: land surface phenology based crop maps for the continental united states 2000 2018 about 231 m

description: This data collection gives annual crop type maps for the continental United States from 2000 to 2018 at about 231 m, derived from MODIS land surface phenology, as a companion to the paper "Mapping crops within the growing season across the United States" (Remote Sensing of Environment, 2020). The Zenodo record lists one NetCDF crop map per year, a legend CSV and further files (20 in total), with validation metrics and method in the paper. Version 1.0 was published on 9 October 2019 by Venkata Shashank Konduri, Jitendra Kumar, William Hargrove, Forrest Hoffman and Auroop Ganguly, with files of about 1.2 GB per year, downloadable and free under CC BY 4.0, with national coverage. Caveats: coarse pixels mix fields, and in-season maps are less accurate than end-of-season ones. For simulation it gives a consistent crop type time series back to 2000 for drought and flood exposure, and crop-specific water and energy demand. Related catalogue records include the USDA NASS Cropland Data Layer, the USGS modeled crop cover 2000-2013 and the Corn-Soy Data Layer.
